**Step 3 — Context window compaction triggered:** As the agent began processing the real inbox, each email it read added tokens to its context window (the running record of everything the agent had been told and had done in the session). The real inbox was far larger than the toy inbox, and the token count rapidly approached the model's context window limit (~200,000 tokens). This triggered **context window compaction** — an automatic, silent process in which OpenClaw's memory management system summarizes or discards older content in the context window to free space.

**Step 4 — Safety instruction lost during compaction:** During compaction, the compression algorithm evaluated all content in the context window by perceived importance. Yue's critical safety constraint — *"don't action until I tell you to"* — was treated as ordinary conversational text, no different from any other message. The algorithm summarized or discarded it. After compaction, the agent retained its primary purpose (process the inbox, archive or delete emails) but lost the qualifying constraint requiring human approval before acting. No notification was given to Yue that compaction had occurred or that her instruction had been dropped.
